A family board for the kitchen wall: today and the next six days from your calendars with the weather for each day, a 24-hour temperature and rain chart, a to-do list and the one-off events coming up in the next five weeks.

Calendars are read from their private iCal (.ics) links, so Google, Apple, Outlook, Proton, Fastmail and any other calendar work. Weather is from Open-Meteo (no key needed).

New here? Leave Calendar links empty and the board shows a sample week, so you can see the layout before connecting your own calendars.

Designed for TRMNL X first; works on the original TRMNL and in mashups.

recipes.d: No more guessing at the night sky.
recipes.about:
Ever step outside on a whim and just happen to catch the northern lights? Neither have we. Aurora is here to help. It reads real space weather data from NOAA and tells you straight: are the northern lights actually visible from where you are, tonight and the two nights after. When the answer is no, it just says so. Pick the abstract halftone chart or a real map centered on your own sky, and choose your voice: plain and factual, or a space physicist who has a hard time staying calm once the numbers turn good. Install (don't Fork!) to receive future updates.

Aurora turns real space weather data into a straight answer: is the aurora actually visible tonight from wherever you live? It reads live geomagnetic activity from NOAA's space weather service and checks it against your own location and the darkness there right now, then tells you plainly whether conditions are good, and for how long.

Beyond right now, it also gives a three night outlook, so you know whether it is worth staying up tonight or better to wait for a stronger night. Every screen shows a verdict, a viewing window when there is one, and which direction to face.

See the forecast as an abstract halftone chart of aurora activity around the pole, or as a real oriented map centered on your own sky. Pick the voice you want it in: plain and factual, or an excited space physicist who can barely contain themselves once the numbers turn good.

Works from either hemisphere, not just the usual northern only aurora tools, and is fully available in English and German. Built entirely on TRMNL's native framework, so it fits any screen size and orientation without extra configuration.

Follow the current Formula 1 race weekend on your TRMNL. The screen leads with the next F1 session and its start time in your time zone, with the weather forecast for the circuit.

A timeline lists every session of the weekend. Upcoming sessions show temperature and rain. Once a session has run, its row lists the finishers in order, as many as fit: practice, qualifying, sprint and race.

More than six days before a race weekend, the screen lists the coming rounds and their dates instead, with the weekend's sessions below.

Beside the timeline is the weekend's news, with grid penalties and other changes that affect a session listed first. On race morning that space shows the confirmed starting grid, and after the race, the race result.

Between seasons, the screen shows the drivers' and constructors' championship standings.

Works in every TRMNL layout, landscape and portrait. Choose metric or imperial units, and a light or dark screen. No account needed.

recipes.d: Charts related to the ERCOT grid
recipes.about:
The "Texas Power Grid" plugin shows a collection of ERCOT information including wind and solar generation, system-wide prices, energy storage resource output, and ancillary services. The display shown on the TRMNL device and be chosen via the dropdown below. This plugin is not affiliated with ERCOT Inc. and uses publicly available data.

This plugin displays charts and metrics for the ERCOT interconnection, the power grid serving most of Texas.

Use the Display option to choose from the following views:

• Wind and Solar: Actual wind and solar generation for today, plus forecasts through the end of tomorrow. Series can be stacked or overlaid.

• System-Wide Prices: Individual plots of hub and load zone prices, comparing today's real-time price with the day-ahead price. An all-prices view summarizes every hub and load zone in a single display.

• Energy Storage: Fleet-wide behavior of Energy Storage Resources (ESRs). Optional toggles add a "net energy" line showing cumulative ESR energy as a proxy for state of charge, and a box plot overlay comparing current behavior to the previous 30 days.

• Ancillary Services: Regulation services over the past two hours.

ann.s: Created by community member . Enable and even the recipes are bigger from Texas.

Apple Health metrics — steps, active energy, sleep, and heart rate — plus today's workouts, synced from iPhone/Watch via the TRMNL Companion app. Data reaches TRMNL only through Companion's on-device HealthKit sync; there's no polling URL or API key. Questions, bugs, or feature requests? Open an issue on GitHub or reach out by email.
Source and docs live in the repo linked below.

Apple Health for TRMNL shows your daily health stats on your e-ink display: steps with a goal progress bar, active energy, sleep, resting and peak heart rate, and today's workouts. When you haven't logged any steps yet, it shows a motivational quote instead. It supports all four layouts (full, half horizontal, half vertical, and quadrant).

Full setup steps, supported metrics, and screenshots are in the README: https://github.com/pradeepbbl/trmnl_plugins/blob/master/apple_health/README.md#how-to-setup

recipes.d: Mirror a PostHog dashboard on TRMNL
recipes.about:
Mirrors one PostHog dashboard on your TRMNL. Sign in to PostHog Cloud (US or EU) to grant read-only access to your dashboards, insights and queries, paste a dashboard URL, and the tiles show up on the device in dashboard order. No third-party servers. Works with PostHog; not affiliated with or endorsed by PostHog.

Show a PostHog dashboard on your TRMNL. Sign in to PostHog Cloud (US or EU), paste the URL of a dashboard, and its tiles appear on the device in dashboard order, refreshed automatically. Useful for keeping product metrics, growth numbers or service health in view without opening a browser.

Trends insights are drawn for e-ink as bold numbers, line charts, bar charts and donuts, following the dashboard's own date range and filters. Other insight types show as a labelled tile. Each page fits six tiles, and all four layouts are supported.

Access is read-only, and your data goes only between PostHog and TRMNL. Not affiliated with or endorsed by PostHog.

Follow your Swiss National League club on TRMNL: league position, the score of the last game, and when and where the next one is played.

Pick your team from the 14 NL clubs, and the plugin does the rest. The full standings appear alongside on the full-screen layout, with your club highlighted. Kick-off times follow your TRMNL time zone, so the plugin still makes sense if you follow your club from abroad.

Available in the three national languages and English, or set to Automatic to follow your account language. Club names adapt too: SC Bern or CP Berne, EHC Biel or HC Bienne, EV Zug or EV Zoug.

Points follow the NL three-point rule: 3 for a win in regulation, 2 for an overtime or shootout win, 1 for an overtime or shootout loss. Teams level on points are separated by games played, then goal difference. Updated hourly from nationalleague.ch. Not affiliated with the National League or the Swiss Ice Hockey Federation.

A digital watch on your TRMNL. Pick a watch face and you are done: the time, the date and, with Weather on, the weather where you live.

Twenty-eight real watch screens, all fully digital (no analog-digital watches), with their marks, screen types and digit styles. The Weather switch adds the weather in each watch's style. The marks are live: RCVD on a strong WiFi signal, LOW on a low battery, DST with your time zone, LT at night. Tides and weather are real, from Open-Meteo.

recipes.d: See the world in a new light
recipes.about:
See familiar places in a new light—and discover worlds you’ve never imagined. National Geographic — Photo of the Day brings remarkable photography to your TRMNL, offering a fresh perspective on the people, places, and wildlife we share our planet with.

Let the photograph take center stage. Enable full-screen mode in the settings to hide the title bar.
WNBA Schedule recipe is a simple app to follow your favorite WNBA team or see all the games from around the league.  Created by Matt Patterson 2026

Top models on the main LLM benchmark leaderboards, up to three side by side. Arena (LMArena) Elo, the Epoch Capabilities Index and Epoch AI's benchmark tables (GPQA Diamond, SWE-bench Verified, FrontierMath, Terminal-Bench, ARC-AGI-2...), LiveBench, and the Artificial Analysis indices with your free key. No server needed. Labels in English or French.

What your Bambu Lab printer is making, with the model's own picture, and the prints before it: print time, filament, material, when each one finished. Everything comes from your Bambu Lab cloud history, so nothing has to run on your own computer.

Setup. Paste your Bambu Lab access token into the field below. To get it, sign in at makerworld.com, open your browser's developer tools, go to Application (Chrome) or Storage (Firefox), then Cookies, then makerworld.com, and copy the value of token. A token lasts about 90 days. When the screen asks for it again, repeat this.

Limits. Prints started from the printer's SD card are not in Bambu's cloud history, so they do not appear. A running print shows up when this plugin's turn in your playlist comes. The plugin reads Bambu's unofficial cloud API, which Bambu may change.

Made by tactus.works.

Ever stood at the door wondering whether to run for the bus or grab a share bike instead? Nearby Nextbike shows you exactly where the bikes are right now.

It puts a live map on your TRMNL, centred on your front door, showing every bike within a twenty minute walk. Walking distances are drawn right on the map, based on your map settings. Filled pins are stations, hollow pins are bikes someone parked on the street, and a small number on a pin means several bikes in one spot. If almost nothing is close by, arrows at the edge of the map point to bikes just out of frame, with the walk time and number of bikes in that direction. A bike four minutes past the edge is still worth knowing about if you were heading that way anyway.

Prefer words to pictures? Set "What the screens show" to *Text*. Instead of a map, you get the closest bike, where it is, and how long it takes to walk there, which works especially well in cities with station based bike sharing.

Works anywhere nextbike operates: over 200 systems in 21 countries. Many run under local brand names, so you may already be using nextbike without knowing it.

Germany:
MyRadl (Munich), KVB Rad (Cologne), VAG_Rad (Nuremberg), Frelo (Freiburg), Bre.Bike (Bremen), VRNnextbike (Rhine-Neckar), KVV.nextbike (Karlsruhe), euregiobike (Aachen), Potsdam Rad, wupsiRad (Leverkusen), UsedomRad, StadtRad Greifswald, MV-Rad, and nextbike in Berlin, Leipzig, Hannover, Düsseldorf, Kassel, Wiesbaden, Marburg, Gießen and the Ruhrgebiet.

Austria:
WienMobil Rad, Stadtrad Innsbruck, city bike Linz, VMOBIL Rad, VVT REGIORAD Tirol, nextbike Klagenfurt and Niederösterreich.

Poland:
VETURILO 3.0 (Warsaw), Łódzki Rower Publiczny, METROROWER, Toruński Rower Miejski, Opole Bike, BIKER Białystok and many more city systems.

Czechia and Slovakia:
nextbike in Prague, Brno, Ostrava, Liberec, Hradec Králové and dozens of smaller towns, plus nextbike Bratislava, Arriva Bike and BikeKI

Weather for anywhere in Germany from the Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), the national meteorological service: an hourly timeline, plus an outlook of up to five days. Missing data reads as a dash, never a zero.

Setup. Search for your town in the Location field, or paste a comma-separated latitude and longitude, then save the form once. The forecast is kept on your account's own timezone, so there is nothing else to set. No API key and no server — TRMNL polls Bright Sky hourly and builds the card in-platform.

Source. The forecast is DWD's, taken through Bright Sky, an open JSON API over DWD Open Data. DWD's terms of use govern the data. Bright Sky is independently operated and not endorsed by DWD, so this recipe cannot promise its availability.

No weather warnings. DWD asks that its attribution be removed from warnings unless they are delivered complete and without delay, which an hourly refresh cannot promise. Forecast only.

Screens. All four layouts are built for TRMNL OG and for TRMNL X in both landscape and portrait. TRMNL X landscape carries a longer hourly timeline than the other two; portrait turns the outlook into a day-per-row list.
